writeup: TIC 97416864 is a candidate eclipsing binary star with an orbital period of 1.1670 days, detected through automated analysis of TESS photometry. The primary eclipse produces a dimming of 1.88%, while no secondary eclipse was detected. The signal achieves a detection significance of 40.9 in the box-least-squares search, with pixel-level difference imaging confirming a peak signal-to-noise ratio of 11.8, though the centroid offset of 4.8 arcseconds from the target location warrants consideration. The candidate does not appear in six major variable-star catalogs, making it a novel find. The machine-learning screening assigned it a score of 0.22, indicating moderate confidence that this represents a genuine eclipsing system rather than an instrumental artifact or false positive. No data quality flags were raised during processing.
